Excel · Statistics · Consumer Behavior Research

Lumiere Research Program — Retail Consumer Behavior

Co-authored a faculty-supervised, mixed-methods research paper comparing consumer behavior at Whole Foods (U.S.) and WinMart (Vietnam), as a Student Researcher in the Lumiere Research Program (Remote, 2025).

Tools
Excel, Google Forms
Data Source
Original survey, 30 shoppers (15/market)
Methods
Chi-square test, t-test
Goal
Compare shopping behavior across markets

Objectives

  • Compare shopping frequency and spend behavior between two retail markets
  • Test for statistically significant differences using chi-square and t-tests
  • Draw conclusions about what drives each market's shopper profile

Key Findings

  • Frequency gap significant: χ² = 12.41, p < .01
  • Spend-per-trip gap significant: t = 4.28, p < .001
  • Whole Foods shoppers: quality-driven, high-spend. WinMart shoppers: price-sensitive, frequent.

SQL · CTEs · Window Functions

Christmas Sales — European Retail Analysis

Analyzed multi-year Christmas sales data from a European supermarket chain to uncover key behavioral and regional drivers of seasonal revenue growth, using SQL (CTEs, window functions) to answer 10 business questions across channel, geography, demographics, and product category.

Tools
SQL Server — CTEs, window functions
Scope
4 Christmas seasons, 10 countries
Dimensions
Country, channel, category, age, gender
Goal
Strategies for marketing, pricing & channel
Q1

Revenue, quantity, cost & profit by Christmas season

SQL query

Revenue, quantity, cost & profit per season (2018–2022)

Finding: Revenue holds steady around $7.0–7.2M per season with quantity near 41.5–42.7K units sold; profit margin is consistent at roughly 77% every season.

Q2

YoY growth for the most recent season vs. the previous year

SQL query

2021–2022 vs. 2020–2021 growth

Finding: 2021–2022 grew +1.93% in revenue, +2.06% in quantity, and +1.93% in profit over the prior season.

Q3

YoY revenue growth trend across all seasons

SQL query

Season-over-season revenue growth

Finding: Growth was uneven: +1.53% in 2019–2020, a −3.16% dip in 2020–2021, then a +1.93% recovery in 2021–2022.

Q4

Revenue share by purchase channel per season

SQL query

In-store vs. Online vs. Xmas Market by season

Finding: In-store dominates every season at roughly 64–68% of revenue, with Online and Xmas Market splitting the remainder fairly evenly.

Q5

Revenue by country and by city

SQL query

Revenue by country, descending

Revenue by city, descending

Finding: Sweden leads by country ($3.78M), just ahead of Netherlands and Germany. Malmö is the top individual city ($1.32M), followed by Gothenburg and Stockholm.

Q6

Countries ranked by revenue growth (most recent season)

SQL query

Country growth rank, 2021–2022 vs. 2020–2021

Finding: Austria (+12.4%) and the UK (+11.8%) grew fastest, while France (−8.4%) and Sweden (−6.2%) declined despite Sweden's overall revenue lead.

Q7

Revenue share by age group, gender, and purchase method

SQL query

Age group / gender / purchase method breakdown

Finding: The 1–11 age group leads at 38.9% of revenue; female shoppers slightly outspend male (50.6% vs 49.4%); in-store still accounts for 64.7% of revenue overall.

Q8

Purchase & payment method within each age group

SQL query

Channel and payment mix by age group

Finding: In-store share falls as age rises (74% for ages 1–11 down to ~58% for 18+). Cash dominates for the youngest group (86%), while Credit Card leads for teens and adults.

Q9

Sales by product category and by product

SQL query

Category and product-level revenue, quantity & margin

Finding: Toys is the top category by revenue ($4.46M) with a ~77% margin; the Barbie Doll is the single best-selling product.

Q10

Shopping patterns by day of week and hour of day

SQL query

Revenue & orders by weekday (gender) and by hour

Finding: Female shoppers peak on Sunday and Monday. Revenue climbs steadily through the morning hours, picking up sharply from hour 7–8 onward.

Loan & Deposit Portfolio Dashboard (KPIM)

Built a two-page executive Power BI dashboard for a bank's loan and deposit portfolios — one page analyzing outstanding loan balances by credit risk, the other analyzing deposit balances by liquidity and funding stability — with Field Parameters, bookmarks, and buttons for interactive drill-down.

Tools
Power BI, DAX (CALCULATE, CLOSINGBALANCEMONTH, SAMEPERIODLASTYEAR)
Data Source
KPIM banking dataset — loan, deposit, customer, branch, product, time tables
Method
Field Parameters, bookmarks/buttons, YoY DAX measures
Goal
Track credit risk vs. funding stability side by side

Dashboard overview — Net Interest Income, deposit & loan balances by department, segment, branch, and product

Objectives

  • Track ending and monthly-average loan balances with YoY growth, by branch, product, and customer segment
  • Track deposit balances by channel, term, and account type to monitor funding liquidity
  • Let users toggle between metrics and drill from branch down to product or customer level

Key Findings & Features

  • KPI cards for ending/average loan & deposit balances plus YoY growth %
  • Trend charts benchmarked against the prior year
  • CASA vs. term-deposit mix trend, highlighting funding stability shifts
  • Branch-level matrix with drill-down into product or customer
